title: Which System of Record Owns Payments-Gateway Oncall (variant)
scenario_text:
Radial operates its production services under a strict ownership model. The Radial Configuration Management Database (CMDB), maintained by the Platform Reliability Office, is the authoritative system of record for service ownership. The engineering wiki hosts a companion 'Oncall Runbook Index' that is expected to mirror the CMDB but is manually maintained by Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and occasionally lags the CMDB.

The company Standard 'ENG-3.2 Incident Response' states: 'When the CMDB and any secondary directory disagree about service ownership, the CMDB record governs.' The standard has been in force for two years and is unchanged as of last quarter.

At 03:14 UTC, PagerDuty fires a P1 for the payments-gateway service after error rates cross 3% for five minutes. The incident commander opens the Oncall Runbook Index in Confluence and sees 'payments-gateway — primary responder: Checkout Reliability (last edited February).' The CMDB entry for payments-gateway now lists the primary owner as Payments Platform, updated on August 21 by the Platform Reliability Office with the change ticket CHG-8842 attached ('service ownership transfer from Checkout Reliability to Payments Platform, effective immediately'). The Confluence runbook has not yet been updated to reflect the transfer.
question: PagerDuty just fired a P1 for the payments-gateway service. Which team should the incident commander page for primary response?
choices: Payments Platform — the CMDB is the authoritative source of service ownership at Radial.
Checkout Reliability — the runbook in Confluence still names them as the responder.
Both teams simultaneously, since the sources disagree and time is critical.
Neither team; page the on-call SRE manager and let them route it after triage.
changed_fact: In the variant, the CMDB migration record shows ownership of payments-gateway was transferred from Checkout Reliability to Payments Platform on August 21 — before this P1 fires — with the corresponding runbook update still pending.
